records.name: Pig Iron Theatre Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater ensemble that makes new performance work, trains performers at its own school, and rents its studios to other artists.
records.what_you_do: Take training through Pig Iron School, come to a student showing or a public show, or attend the Lecoq Symposium or the yearly benefit. The company also lists jobs and internships.

schedule.text: Shows, student showings and events are listed by date on the company website. Class times were not shown on the pages read.

locations.label: Company address (from IRS and Cultural Fund records)

cost.text: No prices were shown for classes or tickets on the pages read.

first_step.how: Look up the Pig Iron School training on the company site, or come to a public show or student showing to see the work first.
first_step.basis: Shows and student showings are open to the public and listed by date; the way into the school was not spelled out on the pages read.

records.notes: The company's own pages showed no street address, and the public email is hidden on the site, so it was not copied. The street address comes from IRS and Cultural Fund records. Devised theater and training school: no exact interest tag exists, so interests is empty. The newest dated item is 'A Day Celebrating Dito' on 2026-09-27 at Miller Theater.

records.name: Second State Press
records.summary: A nonprofit printmaking studio in Philadelphia that teaches hand printing methods, from stone lithography to screen printing, and lets members use the studio.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a printmaking workshop (beginners and experienced printers both welcome), become a studio member, or come to the exhibitions and Second Thursday events.

schedule.text: Workshops are listed by date through early November, such as an intro to riso printing on October 11 and a color woodcut workshop on October 17 to 18. The workshop listings do not show a year. Second Thursday events and exhibitions are listed by date.

cost.text: Prices were not in the visible page content. Check each workshop listing.

first_step.how: Sign up for an intro workshop on the studio site, such as the intro to riso printing on October 11, or come to a Second Thursday to see the studio.
first_step.basis: The site says beginners are welcome and lists intro workshops with dates.

records.notes: The page read was cut short and showed no street address, email or phone. The address comes from Cultural Fund and IRS records. The newest dated items are October 8, 2026 events.

records.name: Taller Puertorriqueño
records.summary: A Puerto Rican arts and culture center in North Philadelphia that shows art, runs youth and family art programs, and keeps an archive on Puerto Rican history in the city.
records.what_you_do: Join an after-school or summer art program, come to a hands-on art workshop or a guided tour, see an exhibition or a public talk, or join as a member. The site has a Get Involved page for volunteers.

schedule.text: Programs and exhibitions run on dates listed on the site. Upcoming: a fundraising dinner on October 10, 2026 at 6 pm, the Latinas Writing Horror session on October 14, 2026 at 7 pm, and the exhibition En Su Sitio, which runs September 11 to November 14, 2026. After-school and camp times were not shown.

cost.text: No prices shown for classes, tours or exhibitions. The fundraising dinner sells tickets through a link, with no price listed.

first_step.how: Call 215.426.3311 or email info@tallerpr.org to ask about the after-school or summer programs, or come to the next public event.
first_step.basis: The site lists youth programs and public events, and gives a phone number and email for questions.

records.notes: Posts on the site show no publish dates, so status rests on upcoming dated events. The Get Involved volunteer page was not read in detail. The audience community tags reflect the center's stated mission.

records.name: The Halide Project
records.summary: A volunteer-run nonprofit in Kensington with a community darkroom for film and historic photography, plus workshops and exhibitions that show the work.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member and use the darkroom (new members start with an orientation), book darkroom time by the day, take a workshop, or come to an exhibition or virtual talk. The Get Involved page lists ways to help.

schedule.text: Darkroom use is booked online through member and day rate pages. Hours and workshop dates were not shown on the pages read.

cost.text: No prices shown for membership, day rates, workshops or events.

first_step.how: Email info@thehalideproject.org to ask about the New Member Orientation, then book darkroom time through the site.
first_step.basis: The site has a New Member Orientation step and a day rate option, so there is a clear way in.

records.notes: The site has no dated events, news or posts, so status is probably active rather than active. Volunteer details were not spelled out on the page read. A second check of its workshop and event sections also found no dates.

records.name: Tiny WPA
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that brings youth and adults into designing and building play spaces, public amenities and neighborhood improvements.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the Ways to Help page, join the Building Hero Project for ages 14 and up when new dates open, or donate.

schedule.text: Building Hero Project dates are coming soon, according to the site. Volunteer times were not listed. The office hours on the site are Monday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm.

cost.text: Program fees were not shown. The Build Your Own public space guide is a free download.

first_step.how: Sign up for the Tiny WPA newsletter to hear when Building Hero Project dates open, or use the Ways to Help page to volunteer.
first_step.basis: Volunteering and the newsletter are open to the public and listed, but program dates are not posted yet.

records.notes: The newest dated item found is a 2023 reference to a planned project. The pages carry no full dates, so status is unknown even though the site works. The batch address (3021 W Stiles St, IRS records) differs from the site address (3145 West Jefferson St). The site address is used here; the owner may want to confirm which is current. A second check of the homepage and its news and blog links found no full dates after 2023.

records.name: Urban Creators
records.summary: A North Philadelphia nonprofit working on food, art and learning since 2010. It runs Life Do Grow, an urban farm with a public park, an outdoor classroom and an arts space.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on a farm or service day, or schedule a group service project. Come to public events the group runs or joins, or join the email list. Past community workshops covered medicinal herbs.

schedule.text: The site lists volunteer days and group service projects but showed no upcoming events. The newest dated item is a Thursday volunteer day on 2024-10-31; the year is inferred from the weekday.

locations.label: Life Do Grow farm and creative space

cost.text: Volunteering costs nothing. No event or service prices were shown. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Email operations@urbancreators.org to ask about the next volunteer day, or use the volunteer link on the site to sign up.
first_step.basis: The site invites individuals and groups to volunteer and gives a contact address, but no beginner program is described.

records.notes: The newest dated items come from an embedded feed: volunteer days on Wednesday 10/30 and Thursday 10/31 and a festival on Saturday 10/12. The weekdays match 2024, so the year is inferred from them, and status is probably active rather than active. The events page showed no upcoming events. The site gives the address as a range; the batch record lists 2316 N 11th St.

records.name: Wagner Free Institute of Science
records.summary: A free natural history museum and science education institution in North Philadelphia, founded in 1855, with a Victorian-era specimen hall of more than 100,000 items and regular talks and courses.
records.what_you_do: Visit the museum for free and walk through the specimen hall, come to a Weeknights at the Wagner talk or the First Saturday Open House, take an evening course, or join as a member.

schedule.text: The museum is open Tuesday to Friday, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm, and on the first Saturday of the month, noon to 4 pm. The site lists two different Saturday season ranges, so check before a visit. Talks are listed by date, such as October 22, 2026 at 6 to 7:30 pm.

cost.text: Museum admission is free. Visits are booked in advance online.

first_step.how: Come to the free museum hours, or register for the October 22, 2026 Weeknights at the Wagner talk on the institute's site.
first_step.basis: Admission is free and the talks and open house are open to the public, but the site does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: The museum is on the second floor and requires stairs; the site sends accessibility questions to the institute's email. The newest dated item is the 2026-10-07 Lantern Slide Salon.

records.name: Directors Gathering
records.summary: A community for theater directors in Philadelphia that holds free salons and gatherings where directors look at their process, try projects they might not otherwise attempt, and meet each other.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free salon or community gathering in person or on Zoom, sign up for the free Basic membership for event access and digital resources, or donate.

schedule.text: Events are listed by date. The newest dated event is September 21, 2026, 6 to 8 pm, in person in Philadelphia. Summer Salon Series sessions are free. The site says a longer membership relaunch is planned for 2026.

cost.text: The events shown are free and the Basic membership is free. Donation amounts are not listed.

first_step.how: Sign up for the free Basic membership, or RSVP for the next free event on the Directors Gathering site (some events ask for an RSVP by a set date).
first_step.basis: Events are free and open to the public, and the site explains how to RSVP and join the free tier.

records.notes: No public email or phone was readable on the page read. The website is listed on the September 21 event flyer. There is no exact interest tag for a theater director community, so interests is empty. The Basic membership tier launched in March 2025.

records.name: Jazz Bridge Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps jazz and blues musicians in the Philadelphia area through hard times, pays musicians for neighborhood concerts, and gives audiences a chance to meet the performers.
records.what_you_do: Come to a jazz or blues concert, volunteer (the site has a volunteer page), or donate and sign up for the newsletter.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed by date: Collingswood on November 19, 2026, Cheltenham on December 2, 2026, and more dates into May 2027. Times were not in the summary read.

locations.label: Office (from IRS and Cultural Fund records)

cost.text: Concert prices were not shown. Tickets are sold through an outside ticketing page.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to the next listed concert (Collingswood on November 19, 2026 or Cheltenham on December 2, 2026), or ask about the volunteer page to help at events.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public with tickets, and the site lists volunteer and newsletter sign-ups.

records.notes: Concerts take place in Cheltenham, PA and Collingswood, NJ, outside the city. Kept as publish because the group serves Philadelphia-area musicians and holds a Cultural Fund grant; the owner may decide whether suburban concerts belong in the directory. No public email or phone was seen. Status is active because the concert calendar runs from November 2026 to May 2027; no past dated post was read.

records.name: Lil' Filmmakers
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches filmmaking and media skills to young people from communities that are underrepresented in film, with mentoring and paid internships for young adults.
records.what_you_do: Apply for a filmmaking program (Story to Screen for ages 11 to 18, or Real to Reel for ages 13 to 24), apply for a paid internship (ages 18 to 24), or fill in the program interest form.

schedule.text: Story to Screen runs 4 to 6 weeks and Real to Reel runs 3 months. Fall program dates were marked coming soon on the site.

locations.label: Office (from IRS and Cultural Fund records)

cost.text: Program fees are not listed. Internships are paid. The site has a donation page.

first_step.how: Fill in the program interest form on the Lil' Filmmakers site, or sign up for the newsletter to hear when fall applications open.
first_step.basis: Programs need an application, and the fall dates were marked coming soon, so the way in is not yet clear.
